questions.question: In a circle, the chords AB and CD intersect each other at point L (internally). If AL = 8 cm, LB = 6 cm and LD = 5 cm, then find the CL.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AL = 8 cm

LB = 6 cm

LD = 5 cm

**Formula used:**

In a circle, for intersecting chords, the product of the segments of one chord is equal to the product of the segments of the other chord:

AL × LB = CL × LD

**Calculation:**

8 × 6 = CL × 5

⇒ 48 = CL × 5

⇒ CL = 48 / 5

⇒ CL = 9.6 cm

**∴ The correct answer is option 4.**

questions.question: In two circles centred at O and O’, the distance between the centres of both circles is 17 cm. The points of contact of a direct common tangent between the circles are P and Q. If the radii of both circles are 7 cm and 15 cm, respectively, then the length of PQ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

The Radii of the two circles are 7 cm and 15 cm

The distance between their centres is 17 cm.

Formula used:

Length of direct common tangent = sqrt {D² - (r₁ - r₂)²} 

Where D = Distance between their centers, r1 = radius of the bigger circle and r2 = radius of the smaller circle

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/726975bbefbb6bc401e04d6b4c972ebcce6acec738379596570646b2b5bc2185.png] 

According to the formula,

Length of PQ = sqrt {17² - (15 - 7)²}

⇒ Length of PQ = sqrt {289 - 64}

⇒ Length of PQ = 15 cm

∴ The length of the direct common tangent is 15 cm.

questions.question: AB is a chord of a circle having radius 1.7 cm. If the distance of this chord AB from the centre of the circle is 0.8 cm, then what is the length (in cm) of the chord AB?
questions.solution:
Given:

Radius of circle = 1.7 cm

Radius of circle = 0.8 cm

Concept:

Chord length using perpendicular distance from the centre = 2 × √ (r2 – d2) [∵ r = radius, d = perpendicular distance]

Calculation:

Length of Chord = 2 × √ (1.72 – 0.82) = 2 × √(2.89 – 0.64) = 1.5 × 2 = 3 cm

**∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: If the radius of two circles be 6 cm and 9 cm and the length of the transverse common tangent be 20 cm, then find the distance between the two centres.

The radius of two circles r₁ = 6 cm, and r₂ = 9 cm

Formula used:

length of the transverse common tangent = sqrt{D²-(r₁ + r₂)²}

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fe586e7da70f1a85def145887633322877e9e7c54f7d80b71a065c9a6ff08321.png]

questions.question: The chord of a circle is equal to its radius. Find the difference between the angle subtended by this chord at the minor arc and major arc of the circle.
questions.solution:
Given:

Chord of circle = Radius of circle 

Concept:

The sum of either pair of opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is 180°.

If 2 angles are made on the same chord, then the angle at the center is twice the angle at the circumference.

Calculation: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ad3d6f3c3e45cd8e5bd4085468ce0bbeab6658fe8239967aaff04fae6b804b5c.png] 

Chord of circle = Radius of circle 

So, ΔAOB is an equilateral triangle (OA= OB = AB)

∠AOB = 60° 

If 2 angles are made on the same chord, then the angle at the center is twice the angle at the circumference.

⇒ ∠AOB = 2∠ACB

⇒ 60° = 2∠ACB

⇒ 30° = ∠ACB

The sum of either pair of opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is 180°.

⇒ ∠ACB + ∠AEB = 180° 

⇒ 30° + ∠AEB = 180° 

⇒ ∠AEB = 150° 

Difference = 150° - 30° = 120°

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: The distance between the centres of the two circles, with radii 3 cm and 2 cm, respectively, is 13 cm. The length (in cm) of a transverse common tangent is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The distance between the centers of the two circles, with radii 3 cm and 2 cm, respectively, is 13 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Length of transverse common tangent = sqrt{d² - (r₁ + r₂)²} 

Where,

d = distance between the centres of the two circles

r₁ = radius of the first circle

r₂ = radius of the second circle

**Calculation:**

d = 13 cm

r₁ = 3 cm

r₂ = 2 cm

⇒ Length of transverse common tangent = sqrt{13² - (3 + 2)² } 

⇒ Length of transverse common tangent = sqrt{169 - 25} 

⇒ Length of transverse common tangent = sqrt{144} 

⇒ Length of transverse common tangent = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: In a circle centred at O, PQ is a tangent at P. Furthermore, AB is the chord of the circle and is extended to Q. If PQ = 12 cm and QB = 8 cm, then the length of AB is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

PQ = 15 cm

BQ = 5 cm

Concept used:

If AQ is a secant and PQ is a tangent, then 

(PQ)2 = AQ × BQ

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/50b7095ed6c57b05cf43e43fbb38978f597c441ef0c777c2638b35e7bf0d0a16.png] 

Let the length of the chord be x.

⇒ (12)2 = (x + 8) × 8

⇒ 144 = 8(x + 8)

⇒ 144 = 8x + 64

⇒ 144 - 64 = 8x

⇒ 80 = 8x

⇒ x = 80 / 8

⇒ x = 10

∴ The length of the chord AB is 10 cm.

questions.question:
If the arc of a circle of radius 30 cm has a length of 19 cm, then the angle (in degrees, rounded off to two decimal places) subtended at the centre of the circle is:

Take pi=(22)/(7)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of circle = 30 cm

Length of arc of circle = 19 cm

**Concept Used:**

Arc length of a circle, l = 2pi rtimes (theta)/(360)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Putting the values in the formula, we get

⇒ 19 = 2 × (22)/(7) × 30 × (theta)/(360)

⇒ (theta)/(360) = (19times 7)/(44times 30)

⇒ theta = (133)/(44times 30)times 360 = (133times 12)/(44) = 36.27º

**Therefore, the angle subtended at the center of a circle is 36.27º.**

questions.question: A chord of a circle is equal to its radius of length 9 cm. Find the angle subtended by it in major segment.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A chord of a circle, which is equal to the radius of the circle.

Radius of the circle = 9 cm

**Concept Used:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fa532f5e3570764db5cfe9670522667105cc94434f326e9b06bc25b274096075.png] 

Theorem, in a circle, the angle subtended by an arc at the center is twice the angle subtended by it at the remaining part of the circle.

**Calculation: **

⇒ The length of chord = radius = 9cm

⇒ It forms an equilateral triangle with each angle at 60°

⇒ The angle subtended by the chord at the center = 60°

⇒ By using the theorem, the angle subtended in the major segment is half of the angle subtended at the center.

⇒ 60°/2 = 30°

**Therefore, the angle subtended by the chord in the major segment is 30°.**

questions.question: The length of the common chord of two intersecting circles is 24 cm. If the diameter of the circles are 30 cm and 26 cm, then the distance between the centres (in cm) is:

Shown above are the two intersecting circles with AB the common chord.

X and Y are the centers of the circles.

The line XY joins the two circles and are perpendicular to chord AB. Hence, they bisect the chord AB at point O.

⇒ AO = AB/2 = 24/2 = 12 cm

AX and AY are the radius of the respective circles.

⇒ Hence, AX = 26/2 = 13 cm and AY = 30/2 = 15 cm

ΔAOX and ΔAOY are right-angled triangles

Hence, AX2 = AO2 + OX2 and AY2 = AO2 + OY2

⇒ OX2 = 132 – 122 and OY2 = 152 - 122

⇒ OX2 = 25 and OY2 = 81

Hence, OX = 5 and OY = 9

⇒ XY = OX + OY

⇒ XY = 9 + 5

⇒ XY = 14

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: From an external point A, tangents AP and AQ are drawn to a circle with centre O. If ∠APQ = 40°, then find ∠POQ.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

From an external point A, tangents AP and AQ are drawn to a circle with centre O.

∠APQ = 40º

**Concept Used:**

The angle between the tangents drawn from an external point to a circle is equal to the angle subtended by the line segment joining the points of contact at the center.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/00353dfe012561af414590108b6d7c31cc576eb823ecaac8f790731cb09f2ff6.png] 

Let ∠POQ be the angle subtended at the center by the tangents.

We know that the angle between the tangents (∠APQ) is equal to half the angle subtended by the line segment joining the points of contact at the center.

⇒ ∠POQ = 2 × ∠APQ

⇒ ∠POQ = 2 × 40º

⇒ ∠POQ = 80º

**∴ The angle ∠POQ is 80º.**

questions.question: Two circles touch each other externally at C. AB is a direct common tangent to the two circles, A and B are points of contact and ∠CAB = 55°. Then ∠ACB is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AB is a direct common tangent

∠CAB = 55°

**Concept used:**

Tangents drawn from a external point on the circle will be equal in length and

their corresponding angle will also be equal

Sum of angles in triangle will be 180°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/12a55d33328c5ac3ae1284c87273914ec7df2b90be972ed298a53a8de1a8eb84.png] 

Draw a line from Point C to Point D lies on tangent AB

⇒ AD = CD (tangents from external point D)

⇒ ∠CAD = ∠ACD = 55°

⇒ Similarly DB = CD (tangents from external point D)

⇒ ∠DCB = ∠DBC = x° (Let)

Now,

In triangle ABC

⇒ ∠CAD + ∠ACD + ∠DCB + ∠DBC = 180°

⇒ 55° + 55° + x° + x° = 180°

⇒ 2x° = 70°

⇒ x° = 35°

⇒ ∠ACB = ∠ACD + ∠DCB = 55° + 35° = 90°

**∴ The correct answer is 90°.**
